ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow nuchal collar and dark-bordered scales. A prominent black subocular streak distinguishes it from similar keelbacks.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Hebius khasiensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, narrow yellow or cream-colored collar on its neck, which contrasts sharply with its dark olive-brown body.
ai.habitat: *Hebius khasiensis* inhabits moist, evergreen montane forests and stream banks in the Himalayas and Northeast India, typically at altitudes between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Khasi Hills Keelback is primarily nocturnal and semi-aquatic, often foraging for amphibians and fish in or near shallow streams and marshy areas.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hebius khasiensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hebius khasiensis* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya and parts of Assam, at elevations between 1,000 and 1,800 meters.
